root_idea.summary: The root centers on good condition and the good or resources acquired, with bird plumage as its concrete image of covering and adornment.
root_idea.development: From feathers as a bird's clothing and ornament, the lexical field extends to human apparel, adornment, provision, property, restored prosperity, and the feathering or repair of arrows; further figurative extensions describe weakness or flimsiness.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested nominal is presented under the normalized citation form رِيش.

senses.definition: Clothing and adornment, metaphorically likened to a bird's plumage.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, the word denotes human apparel or adornment and is coordinated with لباس, rather than literal bird feathers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feather an arrow by attaching feathers to it; hence, to repair or set it right by feathering it.
To provide for, clothe, aid, or otherwise benefit someone; to restore him from poverty, strengthen his means of subsistence, or give him property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from strengthening a wing; the verb may take both a person and the benefit or property supplied.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of shoots or branches, to cover or clothe other branches.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative usage; a less preferred interpretation explains the expression as surpassing the branches in length.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a bird, to shed many feathers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied specifically to a bird in the cited usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To collect property and household goods.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from becoming furnished or feathered.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become rich, prosperous, or well provided with wealth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Intransitive; the cited discussion includes becoming abundant in wealth or competence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become strengthened in one's wing or power through beneficence; to come into a good condition or attain good, with its effect becoming apparent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative Form VIII usage describing recovery or improvement of condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bird whose feathers have grown.
A man possessing property and clothing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative description derived from being furnished or feathered.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The feathers or plumage of a bird, constituting its covering and ornament.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may refer generally to a bird's feathers and can be specified to its wing feathers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Prosperity, good condition, well-being, wealth, or abundance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from covering, furnishing, and good appearance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Property, means of subsistence, household goods, furnishings, and the goods or comforts of life.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the expression أَعْطَاهُ مِائَةً بِرِيشِهَا, the word refers to the saddles, coverings, or other equipment accompanying the camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An intermediary between a briber and the recipient of a bribe who arranges their affair or transfers one party's property to the other.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional social and transactional usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a spear, yielding, weak, or flimsy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative comparison with the weakness or yielding quality of feathers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel, having a weak back.
Of an arrow, feathered, having feathers attached, or having its feathers repaired or set right.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Passive participial description of an arrow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression مَا لَهُ أَقَذُّ وَلَا مَرِيشٌ, having nothing at all.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Idiomatic usage, literally referring to having neither a featherless nor a feathered arrow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a burd garment, figured or marked with designs in the forms of feathers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of patterned cloth.
